newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pernod's Orangina revamps mint soda brand.
newsitem.headline: Pernod's Orangina revamps mint soda brand.

text.p: Orangina, which groups French beverage firm Pernod Ricard SA's soft drinks, said on Friday it is revamping the image of its recently-acquired Ricqles brand to put more sparkle in the minty soda.

The revamp includes a more modern design for the label on Ricqles cans and bottles, which is starting to appear in shops and cafes now, and a television advertising campaign that marks Ricqles' return to the small screen after several years' absence, Francoise Beton, Orangina's communications director, told Reuters.
"We are aiming for a market of young adults, dynamic people a little older than those who drink Orangina," Beton said.

The advertising campaign, run by BBDP, uses actors to play the role of nerve impulses racing to the brain of a Ricqles drinker, who are beaten to their target by the drink's sensation of minty freshness.
Beton declined to reveal the budget for the campaign, which ran for a fortnight from June 13 and began a second showing last night.

Orangina did not pick Young & Rubicam, the advertising agency that conceived award-winning spots for the company's fizzy orange Orangina drink, for Ricqles because the agency already has a large chunk of the Pernod group's advertising, she said in answer to questions.
The new label, a subtle modernisation rather than a complete redesign, keeps Ricqles' signature colours of silver and blue, Beton said.
She said the revamp also includes summer promotions on the product's packaging, tasting sessions in supermarkets and giving away samples of Ricqles in France's railway stations.
The aim is to consolidate the brand's sales of some 10 million francs ($1.7 million) a year in 1997, and to increase sales next year, Beton said, declining to give a sales forecast.

Unlike Orangina, which sells worldwide with annual turnover of some two billion francs, Ricqles is overwhelmingly a French brand, with only five percent of its sales outside France, mainly in Belgium.
Pernod bought Ricqles from Nestle's Perrier at the beginning of this year for an undisclosed amount.
